constraints: dem[d,k]: sum of x into node d for k (+ u[d,k]) = demand[d,k]
flw[f,k]: sum_p y[p,f,k] - sum_{a out of f} x[a,k] = 0 (no inventory)
cap[f]: sum_k w_k sum_{a out of f} x[a,k] - cap_f z_f (- so[f]) <= 0
lnk[a,k]: x[a,k] - demand[d(a),k] z[f(a)] <= 0 (tightening, does not change the optimum)
cls[f]: z[f] = 0 for closed sites; fix[f]: z[f] = 0|1 when a design is locked; closed lanes: x[a,k] = 0 in Bounds
formulation.objective: min sum_f fixed_f z_f + sum_{a,k} (t_out[a,k] + handling_k) x[a,k] + sum_{p,f,k} t_in[p,f,k] y[p,f,k] (+ penalties on slack columns when relax = true)
relaxation: Elastic slack columns are added only when params.relax is true. Penalties per unit: unmet demand 6000 USD/t, capacity overshoot 2500 USD/unit, plant supply overshoot 3500 USD/t, extra open site 3e+07 USD/site.
Each penalty exceeds any feasible marginal cost of the same quantity, so a slack is positive only when the strict model cannot be satisfied.

The relaxation report lists every slack above 0.0005, grouped by constraint family. Individual slack amounts can split differently between alternative optima; the total penalty and status are what is compared.
formulation.summary: Two-echelon capacitated fixed-charge facility location with multi-commodity flow: plants ship to open candidate sites, sites ship to demand nodes, every demand node must receive its demand for every commodity.
variables: x[a,k] >= 0 tons of commodity k on out-arc a (site to demand node)
y[p,f,k] >= 0 tons of commodity k from plant p to site f
relaxed only: u[d,k] unmet tons, so[f] capacity overshoot units, sp[p,k] supply overshoot tons, sm open-site excess

column_order: relaxed only: u[d,k], so[f], sp[p,k], sm
lp_format.names: z{f}, x{a}_{k}, y{p}_{f}_{k}, u{d}_{k}, so{f}, sp{p}_{k}, sm; rows dem{d}_{k}, flw{f}_{k}, cap{f}, sup{p}_{k}, lnk{a}_{k}, mxo, cls{f}, fix{f}
lp_format.note: HiGHS orders columns by first appearance in the file; always map solution values back by column name.
lp_format.number_format: fixed 4 decimals, trailing zeros and dangling point stripped, -0 written 0, no exponent
row_order: fix[f] for all sites when fixed_open is set
lp_format.sections: Minimize / Subject To / Bounds (closed lanes) / Binary (all z) / End; objective lists non-zero costs in column order

penalties.note: Penalties are modelling devices for the relaxation, not costs; they are reported separately from operating cost.

rules: Integers are rounded half up (floor(x + 0.5)) and written with comma thousands separators.
Names are the network short_name in upper case; plants in the list are ordered by tons descending, then plant index; the worst site/city is the largest percentage/tons, then the lowest index.
pct = total supply overshoot / baseline demand (demand_scale 1.0) x 100, integer. worst_pct is the site's overshoot as a percentage of its (scaled) capacity, integer.
sites_word is SITE when the count is 1, else SITES; cities_word is CITY when 1, else CITIES.
Families with nothing to report are skipped; sentences follow the order supply, capacity, unmet, open_sites.

templates.capacity: {count} {sites_word} WOULD HAVE TO HANDLE {units} UNITS MORE THAN THEY CAN; WORST: {worst} BY {worst_pct}%.
templates.open_sites: {n} {sites_word} MORE THAN THE LIMIT OF {limit} WOULD HAVE TO OPEN.
templates.supply: THE PLANTS WOULD HAVE TO MAKE {total} T MORE THAN THEY CAN ({pct}% OF DEMAND): {list}.
templates.unmet: {tons} T OF DEMAND WOULD GO UNSERVED AT {count} {cities_word}; WORST: {worst} {worst_tons} T.

browser.time_limit_rule: Pass time_limit 10 to highs@1.15.3 in the worker. Measured with this build: on a time-out Status is 'Time limit reached'; ObjectiveValue is Infinity when no incumbent exists (take the error path) and the incumbent objective otherwise, with Columns holding the incumbent. highs-js returns no MIP gap, so the gap is NOT available from the solve: show 'GAP UNKNOWN' unless the params equal a preset, then (objective - lp_relaxation_bound_usd) / objective from that preset. A time-limited result is never labelled Optimal and never compared for parity.

solver.browser_note: Python executed here; the browser build is exercised by tests/parity (node, same wasm build). Solve time in the browser is machine-dependent and reported in docs/TESTING.md.
